nodes.text: Still with us, waker? Good. The green suits you.

choices.text: Tell me about the Waking Ring.
Who should I see before I go?
I'm ready for the road east.

nodes.text: Five stones, older than any map of them. They sleep for a week or a season, then one dawn the frost melts off them in a ring and someone new is standing where you stood. _Out in the deep wilds stand ruined gates that hum a colder note — cousins to our stones, I fear. One hums and one breathes, and I trust the one that breathes._

*Bryn* for your arms — south yard. *Iona* for your stomach — the fire by the cottage. *Fen* will talk your ear off about benches and what a log becomes if you ask it nicely. And *Hobb* will let you milk Bess if you stand there looking useful. Small village, full day.

Then hear the send-off: you woke with nothing, and look at you — armed, fed, and upright. Take the lane east over the brook and keep the sunrise ahead of you. The frontier grows teeth the farther you walk, but the *wayfarers* keep lantern-lit waystations along the old ways — rest often. And take this — {item:coins} — every road is shorter with a jingle in it. The Ring chose a good one this time. Off you go.
East over the bridge, past the last lamp, and the world is yours to name. Watch for wayfarer lanterns when the light goes. And eat something before you set out — pride is not a meal.
